stories.headline: Runable raises $21M to expand AI agents for building and growing businesses

sources.title: Runable hits $21M to bet AI agents can go from building businesses to growing them

stories.what_happened: Runable announced a $21 million funding round aimed at developing AI agents that can create and scale businesses. The company reported that over the past 90 days it processed more than 1 trillion tokens, with 60‑70% of that usage coming from paying customers.
stories.why_it_matters: The funding signals investor confidence in AI‑driven business automation, and the high proportion of paid token usage suggests strong commercial demand for Runable's services, indicating a shift toward monetized AI agent platforms for enterprise tasks.

stories.developer_impact: Developers may need to adopt AI‑assisted coding workflows, incorporate verification systems, and adjust to AI‑produced code that can be widely deployed, potentially changing testing, maintenance, and code review practices.
stories.headline: AI-generated 1M lines of code refined into reliable software used by millions
stories.what_happened: An AI system wrote roughly one million lines of code and, over several months, refined it into a reliable software product that is now running on millions of developer machines, according to a quoted source.
stories.why_it_matters: The result demonstrates that AI can produce and maintain large, production‑grade codebases, suggesting a shift in how software can be created and scaled, and raising questions about verification and oversight of AI‑generated code.

stories.headline: Z.ai announces Ox Alpha GLM-series model and plans to release its weights

sources.title: Z.ai confirms Ox Alpha is a new GLM-series model and will release its weights

stories.what_happened: Z.ai confirmed that Ox Alpha is a new model in the GLM series and said it will make the model's weights publicly available.
stories.why_it_matters: Making the weights available lets researchers and engineers run the model locally, potentially accelerating development and competition with other large language models such as DeepSeek.

stories.headline: Giga-Embeddings introduces a 10 B‑parameter Mixture‑of‑Experts encoder for fast, high‑quality text embeddings

sources.title: Giga-Embeddings: Mixture-of-Experts Encoders for High-Throughput Text Embeddings

stories.what_happened: The paper presents Giga-Embeddings, a family of text‑embedding models that combine strong retrieval quality with efficient serving. Its largest model is a sparse 10 billion‑parameter Mixture‑of‑Experts encoder that activates about 1.8 billion parameters per token. Across English, Russian, multilingual, and code MTEB benchmarks, this model achieves the strongest aggregate performance among the family members. The authors also report results on a vLLM inference benchmark.
stories.why_it_matters: A sparse MoE design delivers high‑throughput embeddings while keeping serving costs low, potentially enabling large‑scale retrieval and similarity tasks that previously required smaller or less accurate models. Strong benchmark results across languages and code suggest broader applicability.

stories.developer_impact: Developers may need to adopt the AgentSpec decoding pipeline and adjust their batching logic to leverage the reported efficiency gains, but no specific API changes are detailed in the abstract.
stories.headline: AgentSpec introduces batch-friendly speculative decoding for LLM agents

sources.title: AgentSpec: Speculative Decoding for Batch Inference of LLM Agents

stories.what_happened: The paper "AgentSpec: Speculative Decoding for Batch Inference of LLM Agents" proposes a new system that mitigates the speed degradation seen in existing speculative decoding methods when used with large batch sizes, aiming to improve inference efficiency of LLM‑based agents without sacrificing generation quality.
stories.why_it_matters: If successful, the technique could reduce response latency and computational cost for real‑world applications that run many LLM agent requests in parallel, making large‑scale deployment more practical.
